newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian party cancels Jakarta election rallies.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian party cancels Jakarta election rallies.

text.p: Indonesia's minority United Development Party (PPP) cancelled five election rallies in Jakarta on Friday after it said police had refused permission for a meeting to be addressed by the party's leader.

The Moslem-oriented PPP, one of only three parties allowed to contest May 29 general elections, also halted campaigning in the central Java city of Yogyakarta after windows at its party headquarters there were smashed this week.

The three legal parties, the PPP, the ruling Golkar and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), have agreed to campaign on different days in different parts of the country to avoid violence.

They are vying for the backing of nearly 125 million voters to fill 425 elected seats in the 500-seat House of Representatives in the world's fourth most populous nation. The other 75 seats are alloted to the military, which does not vote.

Golkar, in power for the past 30 years under President Suharto's rule, is seeking to push its share of the vote over 70 percent from the 68 percent it won in the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15.
The PPP campaigned in the main island of Java and the remote eastern Maluku islands and Irian Jaya on Friday.
PPP spokesman Amin Sannang said he did not know why Jakarta police had refused permission for a meeting to be attended by party chairman Ismail Hasan Metareum.
Police spokesmen were not available for comment.
Metareum told reporters the police refusal was detrimental to the campaign.
"We feel that the refusal harms the party...but we haven't made any decision yet on what to do next," he said.
Hundreds of PPP supporters caused traffic chaos in the capital by speeding through the streets on motorcycles and in cars in defiance of a campaign ban on street processions.
Newspapers said PPP supporters in Yogyakarta had lowered the party's flags and removed signs and posters after unidentified attackers smashed windows at its headquarters on Wednesday.
Central Java had been the main focus for political violence primarily between supporters of the PPP and Golkar in the run-up to the start of the three-week election campaign last Sunday.
The official Antara news agency said on Friday police in another central Java town, the PPP stronghold of Pekalongan, had detained eight people after a clash involving political rivals on Wednesday.
Residents in Pekalongan earlier said 18 people were injured in clashes between supporters of Golkar and the PPP, but there have been no reports so far of major violence in the campaign.
